newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - OCT 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - OCT 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- There has been a 47 percent increase in the liabilities of the Multilateral Motor Vehicle Insurance Fund in the year to end-April with total liabilities rising to 7.35 billion rand.
- Rand Merchant Bank financial markets executive director Russell Loubser will take up the reins as executive president of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on February 1.
- SA Breweries' $413 million international share offering, completed on Wednesday, is this year's largest single emerging markets private-sector issue.
- South Africa's inflation rate in September rose sharply to 8.4 percent from 7.5 percent in August -- slightly higher than expected -- as food prices took their toll.

- Worldwide African Investments, one of the key players in the National Empowerment Consortium, has submitted a bid for Johnnic shares worth 500 million rand, financed by three of South Africa's largest life insurance companies.

- South African Airways [SAA.CN] may be forced to cut the Johnnesburg to Cape Town leg of 13 international flights a week if the South African Revenue Services insists on stopping it from taking on domestic passengers during the hour-long stop the flights make at Johannesburg.
- The consumer price index hit a 14-month high of 8.4 percent last month, pushed up by a sharp rise in food prices.

- South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said he would advise government to apply for a loan from the International Monetary Fund if there were no signs of the country's balance of payments improving over the next few months.

- Russell Loubser, the executive director in charge of financial markets at Rand Merchant Bank, has been appointed to succeed Roy Andersen as the executive president of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
- Master Fridge Ltd has received a 23.9 million rand cash injection from NSA Investments Ltd .
- Ismail Mahomed -- who, when he appeared as an advocate in the Appeal court, was forced by apartheid to leave the borders of the Orange Free State before dark -- is South Africa's new Chief Justice.
- The Cabinet has approved a draft law providing for cash payouts for members of the non-statutory forces Umkhonto we Sizwe and the Azanian People's Liberation Army.
